      "observations": [
        "The complete one-line owned diff adds existingHdr.forget(hdr) before the successful early return when the header has no Offline flag. The other successful path already transfers that same header after deleting offline content and clearing the flag.",
        "The old IDL promises an existing non-detached header. The registered callback supplies a Rust getter_addrefs wrapper returning Result<StaleMsgDbHeader, nsresult>; the caller uses result? to populate fields and signal existing/detached completion. NS_OK without setting the output does not satisfy that header-returning contract.",
        "The primary Bug reports Protocol(XpCom(NS_OK)) and attributes it to the unset fast-path output. The owned source directly establishes the missing transfer and its correction; the upstream getter_addrefs implementation and a reproduced warning were not examined.",
        "At the fixed accepted revision the implementation has moved to ExchangeMessageSync. OnMessageUpdated now accepts header fields and returns status, changes a found header internally, conditionally deletes offline content, notifies listeners and commits. Rust now returns Result<(), nsresult> and falls back to creation only for NS_MSG_MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND. This later contract must not be described as the old one-line out-parameter fix.",
        "No tests changed. Checked the local guard, ownership transfer, listener registration, IDL, Rust result consumer and later callback shape. No sync or test was executed.",

      "observations": [
        "All four owned Thunderbird paths and the complete historical diff were read, including every line of the 865-line new test file. This is eligible human functionality and tests, not a size-based exclusion. Production integer conversion and debug behavior change alongside the unit suite and localized error entry.",
        "Historically integer previously returned any non-NaN number unchanged. The new Number.isInteger guard returns existing integers; other numeric non-NaN values go through Math.trunc; other inputs still use parseInt. The suite explicitly expects Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY unchanged. The name does not establish finite or safe-range validation. integerRange converts first and then rejects values outside its caller-supplied bounds.",
        "The fixed module has been renamed to InputSanitizer.sys.mjs and later migrated to Fluent/Error. The integer and integerRange blocks match the owned algorithms after error-ID renaming. Their current consumers separately show XML incoming ports and nonempty manual numeric ports using 1–65535 bounds; security and auth selectors use integer. This study does not audit those later rename/migration entries or all callers.",
        "The owned table covers primitive values, null/undefined, arrays, objects, functions, email/hostname/IPv4/IPv6 examples, coercions and HTTP/data URL expectations. The generic helper explicitly checks that each scenario supplies an expected result for every requested method. Direct successful calls use scalar strictEqual. The error helper checks a localized message prefix and an AccountCreationUtils.Exception instance, not the private MalformedException constructor itself.",
        "The original error factory looked up a properties key before constructing its exception, so the new emailaddress_syntax.error entry lets the suite check the intended malformed-email error instead of an unrelated missing-key error. kDebug changes to Cu.isInAutomation and appends the bad input, explaining the prefix comparison. The current accepted helper separately resolves Fluent strings, then tests Error.isError and the message prefix; it is async because of localization, not because the sanitizer call became async.",
        "The Boolean JSDoc adds intended true/false conversion wording and corrects translate mapping to object. Current Boolean code still uses loose comparisons to the two string literals; this description should not be treated as proof that only primitive string inputs are possible. The selected matrix does not exhaust custom coercion objects, negative infinity, Symbols or every URI/hostname shape. URL fixture strings are inert expected values, not executed content.",
        "All 11 owned assertion call sites, including shared helper calls, have nonempty expected-behavior messages containing should or Should. No missing or empty assertion message was found in the changed test. CASES is input data, named tasks invoke one method, and for...of loops keep returned values and error actions visible. Early-return branches and logical groups were checked separately; subtestSanitizer could use a continue after the throws case to flatten its else, as a scoped readability suggestion.",
        "The registered complete Bug 2006369 and complete D276678 context were read. The reviewer proposed Fluent support and a new Fluent string but explicitly made it nonblocking. The author deferred that migration and explained the missing-key-error problem; the owned source retains properties. Later fixed Fluent code is separate evidence, not adoption by Done or approval. The parent link to the OAuth patch was incidental and removed, so no code dependency is inferred.",
        "The full review has five actual submitted inlines, zero summary edits and zero test-plan edits. Try/build links are historical unopened locators; no unit suite, local lint, localization, setup UI or input-safety experiment ran.",
        "Complete Bug 2006369 current 0–2, attachment metadata, all activity and footer were read during this C collector and reused without another browser visit. It explicitly mentions integer behavior as well as added tests.",
        "Complete retained D276678 creation-to-final timeline, all five actual submitted inline bodies and zero summary/test-plan edits were read for this join. The author explicitly says its stack is incidental, not a direct dependency on D275581.",
        "The proposed Fluent variant and new Fluent file were nonblocking review requests. The author defers the migration and says expecting a missing-string error would test the wrong thing. The owned patch adds a properties key and removes its final period to match nearby errors. Fixed Fluent code is a later phase; Done and acceptance are not evidence the owned patch adopted the proposal.",
        "The review links Try and reports completed remote builds, then closes by the owned landing. Those jobs were not opened, and no local test or lint ran. Source proof and direct assertions establish only the contracts recorded above."
